title: "30-60-90 Day Plan — Template and Worked Examples"
owner: "Ananya Krishnan, Director - Learning & Development"
last_updated: 2026-02-04
version: 2.1
---

# 30-60-90 Day Plan

Every new joiner at Nexora gets one. The manager drafts it before the joining date, the
two of you agree it by the end of week one, and it is reviewed at day 30, day 60 and day
90. It lives on PeopleHub → Onboarding → 30-60-90. It is not a formality: the day 90
review is the first formal probation gate and this document is what it is assessed
against.

## Why the three horizons

| Horizon | The question it answers | Failure mode it prevents |
|---|---|---|
| Days 1–30: Learn | Do you understand the system, the client and the team? | Shipping confident changes to a system you have misread |
| Days 31–60: Contribute | Can you do the work with normal supervision? | Staying in observation mode for a quarter |
| Days 61–90: Own | Can you be relied on for an outcome? | Being technically productive but not accountable for anything |

## How to write one that is worth reading

1. **Six to ten items in total, not twenty.** A plan nobody can hold in their head is a
   plan nobody reviews.
2. **Every item has an observable outcome.** "Understand the architecture" is not an
   outcome.  "Present a written summary of the settlement flow at Thursday's stand-up"
   is.
3. **Every item has a date, not a horizon.** "Day 25", not "in the first month".
4. **Name the people.** "Meet ten people" becomes real when the ten are named.
5. **One item should be uncomfortable.** A new joiner who completes a plan without ever
   being stretched has been under-scoped.
6. **The manager owns half of it.** Access, introductions, a first task that is real but
   safe, and time in the diary — those are manager commitments and belong in the plan
   explicitly.

## Template

```
DAYS 1-30 — LEARN
[ ] Complete all seven mandatory compliance courses            by day 5
[ ] Environment set up; full test suite green locally          by day 7
[ ] <client/product> architecture read; written summary shared by day __
[ ] First small change merged end to end                       by day __
[ ] Meet: <name>, <name>, <name>, <name>, <name>               by day 30
[ ] Day 30 review with manager                                    day 30


DAYS 31-60 — CONTRIBUTE
[ ] Own <named module / service / test suite / workstream>     by day __
[ ] Deliver <named piece of work> end to end                   by day __
[ ] Lead estimation for at least two stories                   by day __
[ ] First independent client-facing interaction                by day __
[ ] Day 60 review; buddy programme closes                         day 60

DAYS 61-90 — OWN
[ ] Deliver <agreed outcome> independently and on schedule     by day __
[ ] Improve one thing nobody asked you to improve              by day __

[ ] Join <on-call roster / review rota / interview panel>      by day __
[ ] Onboard or buddy the next joiner                           by day __
[ ] Agree development goals for the rest of the year              day 90
```

## Worked example — Senior Software Engineer (B3),  BFSI,  Gurugram

### Days 1–30

- Day 5 — all seven mandatory courses complete on NexoraLearn.
- Day 7 — local environment running; full test suite green; first pipeline run observed.
- Day 12 — client environment access granted; client payments-data handling module done.
- Day 15 — read the Settlement Services solution architecture document; present a
  one-page summary at Thursday stand-up.
- Day 25 — three "Low" complexity defects picked up and merged.
- Day 30 — met the Delivery Manager,  the client technical lead,  the QE lead, the
  architect and four team members. Notes recorded.

### Days 31–60

- Day 40 — took ownership of the Reconciliation Engine module and its on-call runbook.
- Day 45 — led estimation for two stories in sprint planning.
- Day 50 — ran the first client status call without the buddy in the room.
- Day 55 — ISO 20022 message mapping change delivered end to end: design note,
  implementation, unit and integration tests, review, UAT deployment.
- Day 60 — flaky test count in the module down from eleven to zero.

### Days 61–90

- Day 70 — joined the on-call roster after shadowing two rotations.
- Day 80 — CI pipeline improvement proposed, implemented and measured (build time down
  from 14 minutes to 9).
- Day 85 — Q3 statement-generation enhancement delivered to production.

- Day 90 — buddying the next joiner to the team; development goals agreed for the rest
  of the year.

## Worked example — HR Business Partner (B3),  Bengaluru


### Days 1–30

- Day 5 — mandatory courses complete.
- Day 10 — PeopleHub HRBP modules walked through with HR Operations; reporting access
  confirmed.
- Day 14 — read the last two quarters of attrition, absence and grievance data for the
  supported function; write down the three things that surprise you.
- Day 20 — attend one full performance calibration session as an observer.
- Day 30 — one-to-ones held with all eight managers in the supported function.

### Days 31–60

- Day 40 — own the monthly attendance exception review for the function end to end.

- Day 48 — run the first employee relations conversation with the HR Manager observing.
- Day 55 — deliver the POSH refresher session to one team.
- Day 60 — draft the function's workforce plan for the next two quarters.

### Days 61–90

- Day 75 — handle a grievance at Stage 2 independently, with documented outcome.
- Day 82 — propose one change to how the function runs probation reviews, with evidence.
- Day 90 — own the function's goal-setting cycle communications.

## Review gates

| Gate | Who is in the room | What is decided |
|---|---|---|
| Day 30 | New joiner, manager | On track or needs support; is training complete |
| Day 60 | New joiner, manager, buddy | On track or needs support; buddy programme closes |
| Day 90 | New joiner, manager, HRBP | Formal probation review 1 |
| Day 180 | New joiner, manager, HRBP | Probation review 2 and the confirmation decision |

A "needs support" outcome at day 30 or day 60 is not a bad outcome — it is the system
working. What is not acceptable is arriving at day 90 with a surprise. If a manager has
concerns at day 40, the new joiner should hear them at day 40.

## Related

- Onboarding and Training Manual (HR-MAN-011), section 6
- Performance Review Process (HR-POL-009)
 - Employee Handbook (HR-POL-001), clause 3.4 — probation and confirmation

# Engineering Onboarding Runbook

For engineers joining a Nexora delivery team. Covers the first two weeks. The HR side of
onboarding is in the Onboarding and Training Manual (HR-MAN-011); this is the engineering
side, and the two run in parallel.

> If you are a hiring manager: everything under "Manager prerequisites" must be done
> before the joiner's first day. A joiner who spends week one waiting for access is a
> joiner you lose in month five.

## Manager prerequisites (before day 1)

| # | Item | Where | By |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Hardware requisition raised | NexServe | DOJ − 14 |
| 2 | GitLab group membership requested | NexServe → Access | DOJ − 10 |
| 3 | Jira and Confluence project access requested | NexServe → Access | DOJ − 10 |
| 4 | Buddy nominated and briefed | PeopleHub | DOJ − 10 |
| 5 | Client access request raised with justification | Delivery Manager | DOJ − 7 |
| 6 | First task identified — real, small, reversible | Backlog | DOJ − 5 |
| 7 | 30-60-90 plan drafted | PeopleHub | DOJ − 5 |
| 8 | Team told who is joining, when, and on what | Team channel | DOJ − 3 |

## Day 1 — accounts and machine

Do these in order. Later steps depend on earlier ones.

1. Sign in to Microsoft 365, change the password, enrol MFA in Microsoft Authenticator.
2. Confirm the device shows **Compliant** in NexServe → My Assets. Disk encryption,
   endpoint protection and the DLP agent are pre-installed. A non-compliant device is
   blocked from every client environment, so fix this on day 1, not day 4.
3. Connect to Nexora Secure Access (VPN).
4. Set your Slack display name to your full name. Join `#eng-general`, your site channel
   and your team channel.
5. Log in to GitLab with SSO. Add an SSH key. Confirm you can see the team's group.
6. Log in to Jira. Find the current sprint board. Find the backlog.

## Day 2 — local environment

```
git clone git@gitlab.nexoratech.in:<practice>/<repo>.git
cd <repo>
make bootstrap        # installs toolchain,  hooks and local dependencies
make test             # must be green before you change anything
make run              # starts the service against local stubs
```

If `make test` is not green on a clean clone, that is a bug in the repository, not in
 your setup. Raise it in the team channel — you will not be the only person it has
happened to, and fixing it is a legitimate first contribution.

 Common first-day environment issues:

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `make bootstrap` fails on package fetch | Artifactory proxy not on the VPN route | Reconnect the VPN; check the proxy entry in `~/.npmrc` or `settings.xml` |
| SSH to GitLab refused | Key added to the wrong account | Re-add under GitLab → Preferences → SSH Keys with the SSO identity |
| Tests fail on timezone assertions | Local machine not on IST | `sudo systemsetup -settimezone Asia/Kolkata` |
| Docker containers exit immediately | Insufficient memory allocation | Raise Docker Desktop memory to 8 GB |
| Client VPN and Nexora VPN conflict | Two tunnels claiming the default route | Use the split-tunnel profile documented in the engagement runbook |

## Week 1 — how we work

### Branching

`main` is always releasable. Work happens on `feature/<ticket-id>-<short-slug>`.
Rebase before you open a merge request; do not merge `main` into your branch. Squash on
merge so that `main` carries one commit per ticket.

### Merge requests

- Small. A merge request over 400 changed lines will get a slow, shallow review, and
  that is a worse outcome for you than splitting it.
- Description says **what changed and why**, links the ticket, and lists what you

  tested.  "Bug fix" is not a description.
- Two approvals for anything touching a client-facing API, authentication, money
  movement or personal data. One approval otherwise.
- CI green before review is requested.  Do not ask a colleague to babysit a red pipeline.

### Code review

 We review the change, not the person. Reviewers are expected to be specific and to
distinguish clearly between **blocking** ("this will break in production because…") and
**non-blocking** ("consider…"). Authors are expected to respond to every comment, even
if the response is "not doing this, here is why".

The reviewer is accountable for what they approve. That includes AI-assisted code:
review it,  test it, licence-scan it, and treat it as if you had written it yourself.

 ### Definition of done

A story is done when:  the code is merged to `main`; unit and integration tests cover the
new behaviour; the pipeline is green; documentation or the runbook is updated where
behaviour changed; observability exists for anything new that can fail; and the ticket

carries evidence a reviewer could check without asking you.

## Week 2 — client environment

Client access is never automatic. It needs the client's own approval, a named business
justification, a signed client NDA, and in regulated sectors a client-specific training
module. Expect five to fifteen working days.

Before you touch a client environment:

- Read the engagement's Delivery Operating Model. It records the working hours, the
  shift pattern, the escalation path, the data-handling constraints, and whether
  AI-assisted development is permitted for that client. These vary a lot between
  clients.
- Never copy production data into a development or test environment. Use the masked
  extract or the synthetic generator. This is not negotiable and it is audited.
- Never test a change against production personal data, however small the change.
- Report any suspected personal data breach to security-incident@nexoratech.in within
  **one hour**. That timeline is contractual with several clients.

## On-call

You do not join the on-call roster in your first 60 days. When you do:

 1. Shadow two full rotations first.
2. Read the runbook for every service you will be paged for. If a runbook does not

# HR Glossary

Terms used across Nexora HR policies, PeopleHub and payslips, in plain language. Where a
term has a precise policy definition, the governing document is named — that document
prevails over this page.

---

**Anchor day** — The one working day each week a team agrees to be in the office
together. Set by the team's manager and published a month ahead.
*See: HR-POL-012.*

 **Attendance regularisation** — Correcting a missed or wrong attendance record on
PeopleHub. Seven calendar days to raise it, three a month without HRBP approval.
*See: HR-POL-004 clause 8.4.*

 **Band** — Career level, B1 to B8. Drives approval authority, variable pay percentage,
notice period, travel class and relocation entitlement. It is not the same thing as a
designation: several designations can sit in one band.
*See: HR-POL-001 clause 2.4.*

**Basic Salary** — 40% of annual Fixed Pay at Nexora. Everything statutory is computed
from it: PF, gratuity, leave encashment, notice recovery, LOP.

**BGV** — Background verification. Run by VeriTrust Screening Services and initiated
about three weeks before joining.  Green,  Amber and Red outcomes; Red means the offer is
withdrawn or, post-joining, immediate termination.

**Buddy** — A colleague assigned to a new joiner for their first 30 days for practical
and social integration. Not a mentor, not a manager, and explicitly not the person who
handles performance, leave or grievances. INR 3,000 on completion.

**Carry forward** — Unused Earned Leave rolled into the next leave year, capped at 30
days. Anything above the cap is auto-encashed in the January payroll. Casual and Sick
Leave never carry forward.

**Casual Leave (CL)** — 12 days a year,  credited 3 days per quarter,  maximum 3
consecutive days at a time, lapses on 31 December, never encashable.

**Compa-ratio** — Your CTC divided by the midpoint of your band's salary range. Below
0.85 or above 1.15 needs written justification from the function head at every review.

**Compensatory Off (comp-off)** — Time off earned by working a weekly off or a holiday
at the manager's documented request. 4–8 hours earns half a day, 8+ hours earns a full
day. **Must be used within 60 days of being earned**, then it lapses. Never encashable.
Not available at Band B6 and above.
*See: HR-POL-004 clause 6. Note: the intranet HR FAQ still quotes the old 45-day window.*

**Confirmation** — The decision at the end of probation that makes you a confirmed
employee. Probation is six months. If no decision is recorded within 30 days of the
probation end date, you are deemed confirmed from that date.

**Core hours** — 11:00 to 17:00 IST. When meetings get scheduled and when you are
expected to be reachable, whether you are in the office or at home.

**CTC** — Cost to Company. Fixed Pay plus Variable Pay plus Retirals. It is not your
take-home pay and it is not your monthly salary × 12.

**DOJ** — Date of joining. The clock for leave accrual, gratuity, probation, long
service recognition and increment eligibility all start here.

**Earned Leave (EL)** — Also called Privilege Leave. 18 days a year, accrued 1.5 days per
completed month. The only leave type that carries forward and the only one encashable.

**EAP** — Employee Assistance Programme. Ashray Wellbeing Services, 1800-102-8899. Eight
free confidential counselling sessions per person per year, for you and each immediate
family member. Nexora sees anonymised numbers only.

**Encashment** — Converting unused Earned Leave to cash at (Basic + DA) ÷ 30 per day.
Happens automatically above the 30-day carry-forward cap each January, and on separation
for up to 30 days.

**F&F** — Full and final settlement. The closing account when you leave. Processed
within 45 days of the last working day.

**Fixed Pay** — The guaranteed annual cash part of CTC. Excludes variable pay and
retirals. Your monthly salary is Fixed Pay ÷ 12, before deductions.

**Flexi window** — Start any time between 08:00 and 11:00 IST, provided you complete
eight net hours and cover core hours.

**GMC / GPA / GTL** — Group Mediclaim (INR 5,00,000 family floater), Group Personal
Accident (3 × Fixed Pay, capped at INR 1,50,00,000), Group Term Life (3 × CTC). All
Company-paid. The parental top-up is the only one you pay for.

**Gratuity** — Payable after five years of continuous service: (15 ÷ 26) × last drawn
Basic × completed years. Waived on death or permanent disablement.

**HRBP** — HR Business Partner. The HR person assigned to your function. The escalation
point above your manager for anything people-related, and the person who attends
probation reviews,  grievance stage 2 and PIP opening and closing reviews.

**IC** — Internal Committee, constituted under the POSH Act at each site. Receives and
inquires into complaints of sexual harassment. Contact posh.ic@nexoratech.in.

**IntegriLine** — The independent whistleblowing hotline,  1800-419-6272, 24 hours, seven
languages, anonymous if you choose. Reports go to a third party and are summarised to
the Audit Committee, not to your management chain.

**Late mark** — Arrival after 11:00 IST without a prior exception. Three in a month costs
half a day of Casual Leave; more than eight is an attendance deficiency.

**Leave year** — 1 January to 31 December.  Not the same as the financial year or the
performance year, both of which run 1 April to 31 March. This catches people out every
 year.

**LOP** — Loss of Pay. A day of absence with no leave balance to cover it. Deducted at
monthly gross ÷ calendar days, and it reduces PF for that month.

**LWD** — Last working day. The end of the notice period, extended by any leave taken
during notice unless the function head waives it.

**Normalisation Council** — The forum that checks a rating means the same thing whoever
gave it. Function head, all B5+ managers in the function, HRBP facilitating.

**Notice period** — 60 calendar days at Band B1–B3, 90 calendar days at Band B4 and

above, 30 days during probation.
*See: HR-POL-007 clause 9.1. Note: the Employee Handbook v3.1 and the intranet HR FAQ
still say 90 days for everyone; the Compensation policy of 1 April 2026 supersedes them.*

**Notice shortfall recovery** — What you pay if an approved short notice is agreed:
(Basic + DA) ÷ 30 per day of shortfall.

**On-call allowance** — INR 700 per weekday and INR 1,200 per weekend or holiday day of
roster, plus INR 1,500 per callout resolved outside working hours, capped at two per day.

**PeopleHub** — The HR system of record. Leave, attendance, payslips, goals, policies,
nominations, helpdesk. If it is not on PeopleHub, for HR purposes it did not happen.

**PIP** — Performance Improvement Plan. 60 days, extendable once by 30. Follows a rating
of 1 or a material decline.

**POSH** — Prevention of Sexual Harassment, under the 2013 Act. Nexora extends the same
mechanism and protections to employees of every gender as a matter of policy.

**Probation** — Six months for every new hire, lateral or fresher. Extendable once by up
to three months. Notice during probation is 30 days on either side.

**Retirals** — The part of CTC that is not cash to you now: employer PF, the gratuity
provision at 4.81% of Basic, and employer NPS if you elected it.

 **Sabbatical** — Up to six months unpaid, after five years of service, with a 12-month
service commitment on return. Gratuity service continues to count; leave accrual and PF
do not.

**Sick Leave (SL)** — 12 days a year, all credited on 1 January. Medical certificate
 required above two consecutive days. Up to five days a year may be used for the
hospitalisation of a spouse, dependent child or dependent parent.

**Variable Pay** — The performance-linked part of CTC: 5% at B1–B2 rising to 20% at
B7–B8. Paid annually with the June payroll. Not payable if you have resigned or are
serving notice on the disbursement date.

**Weekly off** — Saturday and Sunday, unless the engagement's Delivery Operating Model
 records a different pattern.

**WFH** — The attendance code for an approved remote working day.  It is a place of work,
not a leave type, and it does not touch any leave balance.

---

*Cannot find a term? hrhelpdesk@nexoratech.in, or PeopleHub → Helpdesk. Suggestions for
additions are welcome and are usually added within a fortnight.*

# Performance Review Process

Document ID: HR-POL-009. Applies to all employees on the Nexora payroll who joined on or
before 31 December of the assessment year.

## 1. The year at a glance

The performance year runs **1 April to 31 March**, the same as the financial year and
deliberately different from the leave year, which is the calendar year.

| Stage | Window | Who acts | System |
|---|---|---|---|
| Goal setting | 1–30 April | Employee drafts, manager approves | PeopleHub → Performance |
| Continuous feedback | All year | Anyone | PeopleHub → Feedback |
| Mid-year check-in | 1–31 October | Manager and employee | PeopleHub |
| Self-assessment | 1–15 April | Employee | PeopleHub |
| Manager assessment | 16–30 April | Manager | PeopleHub |
| Normalisation | 1–20 May | Normalisation Council | Offline, recorded on PeopleHub |
| Rating release and conversation | 21 May – 5 June | Manager | Face to face, then PeopleHub |
| Compensation letters | 25 June | HR Operations | PeopleHub |
| Revision effective | 1 July | Payroll | — |

## 2. Goals

Between four and seven goals. Fewer than four and the picture is too coarse; more than
seven and nothing is a priority.


Every employee carries:

- at least one **delivery** goal — the work itself;
- at least one **learning** goal, aligned to the Individual Development Plan;
- at least one **values** goal, expressed as observable behaviour and not as an
  adjective; and
- for Band B4 and above, at least one **people** goal — mentoring, hiring, buddying,
  internal faculty, or the health of the team you lead.

Goals are written by the employee and approved by the manager. A goal that arrives fully
formed from the manager is a task list, and it will not survive contact with the year.

Goals may be revised at the mid-year check-in. Revising a goal because the business
changed is normal and expected.  Revising a goal in March because it was not met is not.

## 3. The rating scale

| Rating | Label | What it means | Indicative distribution |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | Outstanding | Delivered beyond the role, visibly raised the standard for others | 5–8% |
| 4 | Exceeds Expectations | Consistently ahead of what the role requires | 20–25% |
| 3 | Meets Expectations | Did the job well. This is a good rating. | 55–60% |
| 2 | Partially Meets Expectations | Fell short on some material commitments | 8–12% |
| 1 | Below Expectations | Fell short across the role | 2–4% |

**On rating 3.** More than half of Nexora is rated 3 in any year, including many people
who had an excellent year. A 3 is not a warning, it is not a signal to look elsewhere,
and it is not what a manager gives when they cannot be bothered to argue for a 4.
Managers who describe a 3 apologetically are the single largest source of avoidable
attrition in the two months after rating release.

The distribution is a guide for the Normalisation Council, not a quota to be applied
inside one team. A manager may propose a distribution outside the guide with a written
justification, and the Council is required to consider it on the evidence.

## 4. Normalisation

The Normalisation Council for each function comprises the function head, all Band B5+
managers in the function,  and the HRBP, who facilitates and does not vote.

The Council exists to answer one question: **would this rating mean the same thing if it
had been given by a different manager in this function?** It is not there to force a
 curve, and it may not adjust a rating without a reason recorded against the individual.

A rating may be moved down only where the Council identifies specific evidence the
manager did not weigh. A manager whose rating is moved must be told before the employee
is,  and must be given the reason in terms they can defend in the conversation. A manager
delivering a rating they do not understand is the worst outcome the process can produce.

 ## 5. The conversation

Ratings are delivered face to face, or on video for remote colleagues, never first in
writing. The manager covers, in this order:

1. The rating, said plainly, in the first minute.
2. The evidence — specific work, specific behaviour, specific dates.
3. What would have to be different for the next band up.
4. The compensation outcome, when it is known.
5.  What the employee wants to say.

Do not open with fifteen minutes of context before saying the number. Everyone in the
room knows what the meeting is about and the delay is not kind.

## 6. Outcomes

| Rating | Increment guideline (FY 2026-27) | Variable pay multiplier | Promotion |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | 14%–18% | 1.50× | Eligible |
| 4 | 10%–13% | 1.20× | Eligible |
| 3 | 6%–9% | 1.00× | Eligible on a second consecutive 3 with a readiness assessment |
| 2 | 0%–4% | 0.50× | Not eligible |
| 1 | Nil | Nil | Not eligible; PIP applies |

Additional adjustments sit outside the guideline: market correction where compa-ratio is
below 0.85, critical-skill premium, pay equity correction, and the promotion increment.

## 7. Performance Improvement Plans

 A PIP follows a rating of 1, or a material decline during the year. It runs 60 days,
extendable once by 30.

A PIP must state: the specific gap, in observable terms; the standard to be met; the
support the Company will provide; the review dates; and the consequence of not meeting
the standard.  Fortnightly reviews are mandatory and recorded.  The HRBP attends the
opening and closing reviews.

A PIP that is really a managed exit is a misuse of the process, and it is visible to
everyone watching. If separation is the intent, say so and handle it as a separation.

## 8.  Promotion

Eligibility requires 18 months in the current band,  a rating of 4 or 5 (or two
consecutive 3s with a documented readiness assessment), an open position at the target
band in the approved manpower plan,  and — for B4 and above — clearance by a Promotion
Panel comprising the function head, a B6+ leader from another function, and the HRBP.

Promotion to B5 and above additionally requires completion of NEX-LDR-101 Leadership
Foundations.

Promotions are effective 1 July. Off-cycle promotions need CHRO approval and are capped
at 1% of function headcount per financial year.

## 9. Appeals

An employee who believes their rating was reached unfairly may appeal to the function
head within 15 working days of the rating conversation, and thereafter to the CHRO. The
appeal must identify what was not considered, or what was considered wrongly.
Disagreement with a fairly reached judgement is not, by itself, grounds for appeal.

Appeals are recorded and reported to the ELT in aggregate each cycle.

## 10. Common failures, and what we expect instead

| Failure | Expectation |
|---|---|
| Feedback saved up for March | Feedback within a week of the thing it concerns |
| "You know what you need to work on" | Name it, with an example and a date |
| Recency bias — the last six weeks decide the year | Notes kept through the year in PeopleHub → Feedback |
| A surprise rating | Nothing in the review that was not said earlier |
| Rating the person's potential | Rate the year that happened |
| Rating a long-tenured colleague on habit | Rate against the current role, every year |

# Remote and Hybrid Work Guidelines

Document ID: HR-POL-012. Effective 1 March 2026. Supersedes v1.2 dated 1 April 2025.

## 1. Designations

Every role carries one of three workplace designations, recorded on PeopleHub against
the position, not against the person.

| Designation | Who | Office expectation |
|---|---|---|
| **Site-Anchored** | IT Support, Facilities, Reception, Security, lab and hardware engineering, and any role on a client engagement with a contractual on-site clause | Every working day |
| **Hybrid** | The default for every other role | **A minimum of 10 working days per calendar month**,  including the team's anchor day each week it falls |
| **Fully Remote** | Exception only | None, subject to quarterly on-site visits |

> **Change in v1.4.** The hybrid minimum was reduced from twelve working days per month
> to **ten**, effective 1 March 2026, following the January 2026 workplace survey and the
> ELT decision of 11 February 2026.  Older material — including the Employee Handbook
> v3.1 and the HR FAQ page on the intranet — still quotes twelve. Ten is correct. The
> Handbook will be corrected at its next revision.

## 2. Anchor days

Each team sets one anchor day per week, published by the manager on the team calendar by
the last working day of the preceding month. The purpose of an anchor day is co-location
for the work that is genuinely better in a room: design discussion, planning,
retrospectives, onboarding, difficult conversations, and eating lunch with people you
work with.

 Anchor days are not attendance theatre. A manager who sets an anchor day and then
schedules the whole day as back-to-back video calls has wasted everyone's commute.

## 3. Fully Remote status

Fully Remote is an exception, not a tier. It requires:

- twelve months of continuous service;
- a role with no on-site dependency, confirmed by the Delivery Manager where the role is
  client-facing;
- the written approval of the function head and the CHRO;
- a workspace declaration (see section 6); and
- review every six months, at which the status may be withdrawn with 30 days' notice.

Fully Remote colleagues attend their assigned office at least once per quarter, at
Company cost, and are expected at the annual team offsite.

## 4.  Where you may work from

| Situation | Position |
|---|---|
| Your registered home address | Permitted for all Hybrid and Fully Remote colleagues |
| Another address within India, up to 30 days | Permitted; inform your manager and update PeopleHub |
| Another address within India,  beyond 30 days | Needs HRBP approval; may change your professional tax and payroll state |
| Another Nexora office | Permitted; book a desk on the Facilities tile |
| A co-working space | Permitted only from the approved list; never for client calls involving confidential material |
| Outside India | **Not permitted** without the prior written approval of the CHRO and Legal — it creates tax residency, permanent establishment and data transfer exposure |
| A café, airport lounge, hotel lobby or any public space | Permitted for reading and writing; never for client calls, screen-sharing or anything classified Confidential or Restricted |

## 5.  Working hours when remote

The rules do not change because you are at home. Core hours remain 11:00 to 17:00 IST.
The flexible start window remains 08:00 to 11:00.  You still record attendance — the
PeopleHub check-in through the VPN client covers a remote day, and the day appears as
`WFH` in the leave and attendance ledger.

What does change is the standard of communication expected. When your colleagues cannot
see you, you have to say more:

- Update your Slack status when you step away for more than 30 minutes.
- Post a short written update in the team channel on every remote day. Two lines is
  enough.
- Answer within the working day,  or say when you will.
- Keep your calendar accurate. An empty calendar is read as "available", and that is
  usually not what people mean.

## 6. Equipment, connectivity and workspace

| Item | Provision |
|---|---|
| Laptop and peripherals | Standard kit per HR-POL-001 clause 11.1; the monitor and dock may be taken home with manager approval recorded on NexServe |
| Internet and telephone allowance | INR 1,500 per month, paid with salary against a declaration, no bills required |
| Minimum connection | 20 Mbps down, 5 Mbps up, with a fallback (mobile hotspot is acceptable) |
| Power continuity | A UPS or inverter for the router is claimable once every three years, up to INR 8,000 |
| Chair and desk | Not provided; an ergonomic assessment is available on request through the HRBP, and equipment supported by an occupational-health note is provided |
| Workspace declaration | A short PeopleHub form confirming a workable, reasonably private setup — required for Fully Remote, optional for Hybrid |

## 7. Security when working away from the office

1. VPN on, always, before you touch anything work-related.
2. Screen lock when you step away, including at home. Household members are not
   authorised users.
3. Headphones for every call where client material is discussed.
4. No printing of Confidential or Restricted material outside the office.
5. No personal removable storage on the Nexora device, ever.
6.  No family use of the Company laptop,  not even to print a school form.
7. Video-call backgrounds must not reveal whiteboards, screens, documents or anything
   else you would not hand to a stranger.

## 8. Manager responsibilities

- Publish the anchor day a month ahead.
- Do not treat presence as a proxy for contribution, and do not treat absence as a
  proxy for its lack.
- Run meetings so that a remote participant is a full participant: one person one

  camera, notes in writing, decisions recorded in the channel and not just in the room.
 - Make sure the person who is remote today is not the person who finds out last.
- Check in on the colleague who has not been to the office in six weeks. Not to police
  them — because isolation is the most common thing hybrid working gets wrong.

## 9. When this does not work

Hybrid status may be varied or withdrawn where there is a documented performance
concern, a client contractual requirement, a security incident linked to remote working,
or a persistent failure to meet the monthly office minimum. Withdrawal is a managed
conversation with the HRBP present and 30 days' notice, not an instruction in a message.

## 10. Related documents

| Document | ID |
|---|---|
| Employee Handbook (clause 4.6 — note: quotes the superseded 12-day figure) | HR-POL-001 |
| Leave and Attendance Policy | HR-POL-004 |
| Acceptable Use Policy | ISMS-POL-004 |
| Information Security Policy | ISMS-POL-001 |
| Travel and Expense Reimbursement Policy | FIN-POL-006 |

9.1  After confirmation, either party may terminate this employment by giving written notice of {{NOTICE_PERIOD_DAYS}} calendar days — sixty (60) calendar days for Band B1 to B3 and ninety (90) calendar days for Band B4 and above — or salary in lieu of notice at the Company's option.

9.2  Earned Leave may not be adjusted against the notice period. Leave taken during notice extends your last working day by an equivalent number of calendar days unless expressly waived in writing.

9.3  The Company may terminate your employment without notice or notice pay for serious misconduct as described in the Employee Handbook, including theft, fraud, falsification of records, unauthorised disclosure of confidential information, sexual harassment, physical violence and the acceptance of a bribe.

9.4  For twelve (12) months after your last working day, you will not solicit any employee of the Company to leave its employment, nor solicit any client of the Company that you served in the twelve months before that date.

9.5  On separation you will return all Company and client property, including devices, access cards, documents and data, and will delete all Company and client material from any personal device or account.

10. General

10.1  The age of superannuation is fifty-eight (58) years, calculated to the last day of the month in which you attain that age.

10.2  This letter is governed by the laws of India. The courts at Gurugram, Haryana have exclusive jurisdiction.

10.3  If any provision of this letter is held unenforceable, the remaining provisions continue in full force.

10.4  Please sign and return the duplicate copy of this letter, together with Annexure D, within seven (7) days of the date of this letter. This offer lapses if it is not accepted within that period.

We look forward to welcoming you to Nexora.

Yours sincerely,

Code of Conduct and Prevention of Sexual Harassment Policy
HR-POL-002  |  v5.0  |  Effective 1 April 2026
Confidential — Internal Use Only
Nexora Technologies
Page 6
1. Introduction
1.1 A Message on Purpose
Nexora Technologies holds client source code, client production systems, and the personal data of millions
of end customers. Our clients grant us that access on the strength of a judgment about our character, not
only our capability. This Code exists to make that judgment safe.
The Code cannot anticipate every situation. Where it is silent, apply the following test before acting:
 1. Is it legal? Under Indian law and the law of the jurisdiction concerned.
2. Is it within policy? Under this Code and the policies referenced in Clause 1.4.
3. Is it honest? Would the description you would give of your action match what you
actually did?
 4. Would it survive publication? Would you be comfortable if the action were reported
accurately to your team, the client and your family?
If the answer to any of these is "no" or "I am not sure", stop and ask. The channels are in Clause 12.
1.2 Who This Code Applies To
This Code applies to every director, officer and employee of Nexora Technologies Private Limited, and to
every probationer, Graduate Engineer Trainee, fixed-term contract employee and intern. Contractors,
consultants, vendors and staffing partners are bound by the equivalent obligations in the Third Party Code
of Conduct (LEG-POL-003), which every purchase order and master services agreement incorporates by
reference.
The Code applies wherever you are: at a Nexora office, at a client site, at a conference, at an offsite, on a
client call from home, and on any online forum where you are identifiable as a Nexora employee.
1.3 Your Obligations Under This Code
Every person to whom this Code applies must:
 (a) read the Code and record an electronic acknowledgement on PeopleHub on joining and annually
thereafter, by 30 April each year;
(b) complete course NEX-HR-103 (Code of Conduct and Business Ethics) within thirty (30) days of joining
and annually thereafter;
(c) complete the annual Conflict of Interest declaration on PeopleHub by 30 April;
(d) report a suspected breach of the Code promptly through any channel in Clause 12; and
(e) cooperate fully and honestly with any investigation, including by preserving records.
Managers at Band B4 and above carry the additional obligation to model the Code, to create conditions in
which team members can raise concerns without cost, and to escalate any concern raised with them within
two (2) working days.

2. Integrity in Business Dealings
2.1 Anti-Bribery and Anti-Corruption
Nexora prohibits bribery in every form, in every country, without exception and without a materiality
threshold. No employee may, directly or through a third party, offer, promise, give, request, agree to
receive or accept any financial or other advantage intended to induce or reward the improper performance
of a function.
This prohibition applies to dealings with government officials and to purely commercial dealings. It extends
to conduct that would be an offence under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, the Foreign Corrupt
Practices Act of the United States, and the Bribery Act 2010 of the United Kingdom, each of which applies
to some part of Nexora's client base.
Facilitation payments — small unofficial payments to speed up a routine government action such as a
visa, a licence or a customs clearance — are prohibited without exception, even where they are customary
in the location concerned. If you are asked for one, refuse, and report it to ethics@nexoratech.in the same
day. Where personal safety is at risk, protect your safety first, pay if you must, and report immediately
afterwards; you will not face disciplinary action for a payment made under duress that is promptly reported.

2.3 Conflicts of Interest
A conflict of interest exists where your personal interest, or that of a relative, could reasonably be seen to
influence, or to have influenced, a decision you take on behalf of Nexora. A perceived conflict damages
trust as effectively as an actual one.
Situations that must be declared:
 1. A financial interest above 2% of the equity, or above INR 5,00,000 in value, in a client,
vendor, competitor or prospective vendor of Nexora.

3. A relative — as defined in Section 2(77) of the Companies Act, 2013 — employed by, or

 4. A relative employed by Nexora, whether or not in the same reporting line.
5. Participation in any selection, evaluation, procurement or appraisal decision affecting a

 6. Any outside engagement, paid or unpaid, that uses Nexora time, assets, information or
name.
 7. A personal relationship with a person you supervise, directly or indirectly.
Declarations are made on PeopleHub → Compliance → Conflict of Interest, on joining, annually by 30 April,
and within seven (7) days of the circumstances arising. A declared conflict is not itself a breach; failing to
declare it is.
Personal relationships in the reporting line. A romantic or familial relationship between an employee
and a person in their reporting line, direct or indirect, must be declared to the HRBP within seven days.
Nexora does not prohibit such relationships, but it will restructure the reporting line, the appraisal
responsibility, or both. Neither party may participate in any decision affecting the other's compensation,
rating, promotion, staffing or discipline.
2.4 Outside Employment and Moonlighting
Employees may not accept concurrent employment, a retainer, a consulting engagement, or a directorship
with any other commercial entity without the prior written approval of the CHRO, recorded on PeopleHub.
Permitted without approval:
  passive investment in listed securities, mutual funds and similar instruments, subject to Clause 2.6;
 unpaid teaching, mentoring, academic writing and conference speaking, provided it does not disclose
Company or client information and does not occur during working hours;
 contribution to open-source projects that are unrelated to any client engagement you work on, using
personal equipment and personal time, subject to ISMS-POL-004;
 income from writing, the arts, sport, agriculture and family property;
 unpaid office in a registered non-profit, resident welfare association or professional body.
Approval will normally be refused where the outside engagement is with a client, a vendor or a competitor
of Nexora; where it uses skills, tools or knowledge acquired in a client engagement; or where it would
occupy time during Nexora working hours.
2.5 Fair Competition
Nexora competes on the quality and price of its work. Employees must not:

(a) enter into or discuss any arrangement with a competitor concerning prices, bid rigging, market
allocation, or a no-poach agreement, which would breach the Competition Act, 2002;
(b) obtain a competitor's confidential information by deception, or accept it from a person who is under an
obligation not to disclose it, including a new joiner from a competitor;
(c) disparage a competitor with a statement that is untrue or that cannot be substantiated; or
(d) discuss Nexora's pricing, margins or bidding intentions at an industry association meeting or an

New joiners. A person joining Nexora from a competitor must not bring, disclose or use any confidential
information belonging to the former employer. Hiring managers must brief every such joiner in writing on
the first day and must record the briefing on PeopleHub.
2.6 Insider Trading
Nexora Technologies is an unlisted private company; its own shares are not publicly traded. However,
employees regularly receive unpublished price-sensitive information (UPSI) about listed clients — an
unannounced acquisition, an earnings figure, a system failure, a regulatory action, a large contract.
Employees who possess UPSI about any listed entity must not deal in that entity's securities, must not
recommend that anyone else deal, and must not pass the information to any person who does not need it
for their work. This obligation continues until the information is genuinely public. Breach is an offence under
the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015, and exposes both the individual and Nexora to
prosecution.
Employees on a client engagement designated "Restricted" by the General Counsel are placed on a
restricted list and must pre-clear all personal trades in that client's securities through LEG-POL-007.
2.7 Accurate Records
Every record you create on behalf of Nexora — a timesheet, an expense claim, a status report, a test
result, a defect log, a code review sign-off, a certificate of completion, an audit response — must be
complete and accurate.
Specifically prohibited:
  recording hours not worked, or recording hours to a client or project code other than the one on which
the work was performed;
 submitting an expense claim for an expense not incurred, or for a personal expense;
 signing off a test cycle, security review or code review that was not performed;
 backdating any document;
 creating or maintaining any undisclosed fund, account or asset.
Falsification of records is serious misconduct under HR-POL-001, Clause 15.3 and will lead to termination
in nearly every case.

3. Confidentiality, Data and Intellectual Property
3.1 Confidential Information
Confidential information includes anything not in the public domain that Nexora or a client would not wish
disclosed: source code, architecture, credentials, contracts, pricing, bid material, client roadmaps, incident
detail, unreleased product information, employee personal data, and the fact of a client relationship where
the client has not agreed to a public reference.
Rules:
 1. Access, use or disclose confidential information only for the purpose for which access was
granted.
 2. Do not discuss client matters in public places — airports, cafés, cabs, lifts, coworking
spaces, or on a video call in a shared room without headphones.
 3. Do not store client material on a personal device, a personal email account or a personal
cloud service, and do not print it outside the office.
 4. Do not use one client's material, code or approach for another client. Engagement teams
working for competing clients are separated by information barriers documented in the engagement's
Delivery Operating Model.
 5. Confidentiality obligations survive the end of employment indefinitely.
3.2 Personal Data
Nexora processes personal data as a Data Fiduciary in respect of its own employees, and as a Data
Processor in respect of client end-customer data. The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 governs
both, alongside the client contract and, where applicable, the GDPR.
Every employee handling personal data must:
 (a) process it only on documented instructions from the client or the Company;
(b) collect and access the minimum necessary for the purpose;
(c) never copy production personal data into a development, test or training environment without
approved masking or synthetic substitution;
(d) never use production personal data to test a change, however small;
(e) report a suspected personal data breach to security-incident@nexoratech.in **within one
(1) hour** of becoming aware of it — this timeline is contractual with several clients and supports the
statutory notification obligation; and
(f) complete course NEX-LEG-104 annually.

Employees must not incorporate third-party code, content, fonts, images or datasets into Company or client

3.4 Artificial Intelligence
Use of generative AI is permitted and encouraged within the boundaries of ISMS-POL-009:
 1. Use only the enterprise instances provisioned by Nexora and listed on the NexServe
software catalogue. Consumer accounts, personal API keys and unapproved browser extensions are
prohibited for work purposes.

overrides this clause. The engagement's Delivery Operating Model records the position for every client.

security issues before it is committed. The reviewer is accountable for the code as if they had written it.
 5. Do not present AI-generated analysis, estimates or client deliverables as independently
verified work unless you have verified it.

4. Respect at Work
4.1 Equal Opportunity and Non-Discrimination
Nexora makes every employment decision — hiring, staffing, appraisal, promotion, compensation, training,
discipline and separation — on merit. Discrimination on the basis of religion, race, caste, sex, gender,
gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, place of birth, descent, language, marital or parental
status, pregnancy, disability, age, HIV status, or any other status protected by law is prohibited.
Nexora provides reasonable accommodation to employees with disabilities in accordance with the Rights
of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016. Requests are made to the HRBP and are determined within fifteen
(15) working days.
4.2 Bullying, Harassment and Retaliation
Prohibited conduct includes:
  persistent criticism, humiliation or ridicule, in private or in front of others;
 shouting, abusive language, threats, or intimidating physical conduct;
 deliberate exclusion from meetings, information or opportunities;
 setting objectives that are designed to be unachievable;
 misuse of position to demand personal favours;
 offensive jokes or comments about a protected characteristic, whether or not directed at a specific
person;
 circulating offensive material on Company systems or in team channels;
 retaliation of any kind against a person who raises a concern or participates in an inquiry.
Firm, fair and specific performance feedback delivered with respect is not bullying. A manager is entitled —
and expected — to set demanding standards, to say clearly when work is not good enough, and to hold
people to commitments.
4.3 Substance Use
Reporting for work, or being on Company or client premises, under the influence of alcohol or any
controlled substance is serious misconduct. Nexora offices are alcohol-free except at an event expressly
authorised in writing by the site head, at which responsible consumption is expected and
Company-arranged transport is provided.
An employee who voluntarily discloses a dependency before any incident occurs will be supported through
the Employee Assistance Programme and will not face disciplinary action for the disclosure itself.
4.4 Workplace Safety
Every employee must comply with safety instructions, report hazards and near misses, and participate in
evacuation drills. Violence, threats of violence, and possession of a weapon on Company premises are
serious misconduct and will be reported to the police.

5. Company Assets and Communications
5.1 Use of Assets
Company assets — devices, network, software licences, meeting rooms, stationery, subscriptions and time
— are provided for Company work. Incidental personal use of the device and network is permitted where it
is reasonable in extent, does not interfere with work, does not incur material cost, and does not involve
prohibited content.
5.2 Social Media
Employees are free to use social media personally. When doing so:
 1. Make clear that views are your own. Do not present a personal view as a Nexora position.
2. Never disclose client names, client work, unreleased information, incident detail,
internal metrics, or photographs taken inside a delivery zone.
 3. Do not post about a colleague in a manner that would breach Clause 4.2 if said at work.
4. Only the Marketing team and persons authorised by the CEO may speak for Nexora publicly or
respond to a media enquiry. Forward all media enquiries to press@nexoratech.in.
 5. Do not use the Nexora logo, name or brand assets in a personal capacity without approval.
5.3 Political Activity
Employees may participate in lawful political activity in their personal capacity, in their own time, using their
own resources. Nexora makes no political contributions of any kind and no employee may make one on the
Company's behalf or using Company funds. Do not use Company premises, email, systems or the Nexora
name for political activity.
5.4 Charitable Activity
Nexora supports employee volunteering through the Nexora Cares programme, which provides two
 (2) days of paid volunteering leave per employee per financial year for work with a
registered non-profit. Solicitation of colleagues for donations is permitted only through the Nexora Cares
platform and never through direct or repeated personal approach.

6. Client and Vendor Relationships
6.1 Client Interactions
Represent status honestly. Do not report a milestone as complete when it is not, do not conceal a defect, a
delay or an incident, and do not commit to a scope, date or price without the authority to do so. Where you
have made an error that affects a client, escalate it to your Delivery Manager the same day.
Do not accept an instruction from a client that would require you to breach this Code, Indian law, or the
client's own contractual restrictions. Escalate instead.
6.2 Client Property and Access
Access to a client's systems is granted for a defined scope and period. Employees must not exceed the
granted scope, must not share credentials, must not retain client data after the engagement ends, and
must surrender client-issued devices and passes on rotation off the engagement. Access is revoked within
twenty-four (24) hours of an employee's rotation off an engagement or separation from the Company.
6.3 Vendors and Procurement
Procurement decisions are made on documented evaluation criteria by the Procurement function. No
employee may commit Nexora to a purchase, a licence or a contractual obligation without authority under
the Delegation of Authority matrix (FIN-POL-001). Splitting a purchase to avoid an approval threshold is a
breach of this Code.

7. Disciplinary Consequences
A breach of this Code is dealt with under HR-POL-001, Clause 15. Consequences range from counselling
to termination for cause, and may include recovery of loss, referral to law enforcement, and reporting to a
regulator or client where required by contract or law.
Factors considered are the seriousness of the breach, whether it was deliberate or negligent, whether it
was self-reported, the level of the individual, the harm caused, cooperation with the investigation, and the
disciplinary history.
Self-reporting a breach promptly is a substantial mitigating factor and is recorded as such. Concealing a
breach, or misleading an investigator, is a serious aggravating factor.

8. Statutory Basis and Commitment
This Part is issued under Section 19 of the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention,
Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 ("the POSH Act") and the rules made thereunder. It is displayed at a
conspicuous place at each Nexora workplace and on PeopleHub → Policies.
Nexora is committed to a workplace free of sexual harassment. Every complaint is taken seriously, handled
confidentially, and inquired into by a duly constituted Internal Committee within the statutory timelines.
Extension of protection. The POSH Act confers rights on aggrieved women. Nexora extends the identical
complaint mechanism, the identical protections and the identical procedure to every employee of any
gender, and to persons of any gender identity, as a matter of Company policy. Where a complaint is made
by a person who is not an aggrieved woman under the Act, the Internal Committee conducts the inquiry
under this Policy using the same procedure, and the outcome carries the same consequences, save that
the statutory reporting obligations apply only to complaints under the Act.

9. What Constitutes Sexual Harassment
9.1 Statutory Definition
Under Section 2(n) of the POSH Act, "sexual harassment" includes any one or more of the following
unwelcome acts or behaviour, whether directly or by implication:
 (i) physical contact and advances;
(ii) a demand or request for sexual favours;
(iii) making sexually coloured remarks;
(iv) showing pornography;
(v) any other unwelcome physical, verbal or non-verbal conduct of a sexual nature.
9.2 Circumstances Amounting to Harassment
Under Section 3(2), the following circumstances, if they occur in relation to any act or behaviour of sexual
harassment, may amount to sexual harassment:
 (a) implied or explicit promise of preferential treatment in employment;
(b) implied or explicit threat of detrimental treatment in employment;
(c) implied or explicit threat about present or future employment status;
(d) interference with work, or creation of an intimidating, offensive or hostile work environment;
(e) humiliating treatment likely to affect health or safety.
9.3 Illustrative Examples
The following, when unwelcome, are examples of conduct that may constitute sexual harassment at
Nexora. The list is illustrative and not exhaustive.
  Comments on a colleague's body, clothing, appearance or personal life of a sexual nature.
 Persistent requests for a date, a personal meeting or contact outside work after a refusal.
 Sending sexually explicit images, links, memes, emojis or messages on any channel, including a
personal WhatsApp number obtained from the employee directory.
 Unnecessary physical contact — touching, hugging, patting, brushing past, blocking a path.
 Staring in a manner that causes discomfort; comments about a person's body on a video call.
 Sexual jokes, innuendo or "banter" in a team channel, a stand-up or an offsite.
 Displaying or circulating pornography on a Company device or network.
 Suggesting that a rating, a project allocation, an onsite opportunity or a promotion depends on a
personal relationship.
 Spreading sexual rumours about a colleague.
 Repeated invitations to drink alcohol coupled with comments of a sexual nature.
 Recording or photographing a colleague without consent in circumstances of intimacy.

9.4 "Workplace" and "Employee"
"Workplace" for this Policy includes every Nexora office; any client site, vendor site or third-party premises
where an employee is present in the course of employment; any place visited during the course of
employment including transportation provided by the Company; Company-organised events, offsites,
training programmes and celebrations, including where they involve alcohol; and any digital channel used
for work, including email, Slack, Teams, Zoom, the PeopleHub messaging module, and work-related
groups on personal messaging applications.
"Employee" includes permanent employees, probationers, trainees, interns, apprentices, fixed-term
contract employees, consultants, contractors, staffing-partner personnel and volunteers, whether or not
paid by Nexora, and whether the terms of engagement are express or implied.
9.5 What Is Not Sexual Harassment
Legitimate and respectfully delivered performance feedback, a fair rating, a decision not to promote, a
change in project allocation, the enforcement of attendance rules, and ordinary managerial supervision are
not sexual harassment, even where they are unwelcome to the recipient. Consensual conduct between
adults is not harassment, though it may raise a conflict of interest under Clause 2.3 and must be declared.

A member is removed from the IC where the member contravenes Section 16 (confidentiality), is convicted

their position so as to render continuance prejudicial to the public interest. A vacancy is filled within thirty
(30) days.
A member who is a party to the complaint, who is in the reporting line of either party, or who has a personal
relationship with either party, recuses from that inquiry. The recusal is recorded and a substitute member is
nominated by the CHRO for that inquiry.
10.6 Powers of the Internal Committee
The IC has the powers of a civil court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 in respect of summoning
and enforcing the attendance of any person and examining them on oath, and requiring the discovery and
production of documents (Section 11(3) of the POSH Act).
The Company will provide the IC with such facilities, assistance and access to records as it requires, and
will secure the attendance of any employee whom the IC wishes to examine.

11. Complaint and Inquiry Procedure
11.1 Who May Complain and How
A complaint may be made by the aggrieved person. Where the aggrieved person is unable to make a
complaint by reason of physical or mental incapacity or death, a complaint may be made by the persons
specified in Rule 6 of the POSH Rules, 2013, including a relative, a friend, a co-worker, an officer of the
National or State Commission for Women, or a person who has knowledge of the incident with the written
consent of the aggrieved person.
A complaint may be submitted:
  by email to posh.ic@nexoratech.in, which is accessible only to the Presiding Officers;
 in writing to the Presiding Officer for the site, in a sealed envelope;
 in person to any IC member; or
 through PeopleHub → Helpdesk → POSH Complaint, which routes directly to the IC and is not visible to
HR Operations or the reporting manager.
Six (6) copies of the complaint, together with supporting documents and the names and addresses of
witnesses, are required by Rule 7(1). Where the complaint is received by email or through PeopleHub, the
IC secretary prepares the copies; the complainant is not required to do so.
Assistance in making a complaint. Where a complainant is unable to reduce the complaint to writing, any
IC member will provide reasonable assistance in doing so, and will record that assistance was provided.
11.2 Time Limit
A complaint must be made within three (3) months of the date of the incident, or, in the case of a series of
incidents, within three months of the date of the last incident.
The IC may extend this period by a further three (3) months where it is satisfied that circumstances
prevented the complainant from filing within the original period. The reasons for an extension are recorded
in writing.

11.4 Conciliation
Before initiating an inquiry, the IC may, at the request of the complainant and only at that request, take
steps to settle the matter through conciliation (Section 10).
  No monetary settlement may be made the basis of a conciliation.
 Where a settlement is arrived at, the IC records it and forwards it to the employer, who acts on it. No
further inquiry is conducted.
 Where the complainant informs the IC that a term of the settlement has not been complied with, the IC
proceeds to an inquiry.
 Conciliation is never proposed by the IC, the employer or the respondent, and the complainant is under
no obligation to consider it.
11.5 Interim Relief
At the written request of the complainant, and at any stage before the inquiry is completed, the IC may
recommend to the employer that it (Section 12):
 (a) transfer the complainant or the respondent to another workplace or another team;
(b) grant the complainant leave of up to three (3) months, which is in addition to the leave the
complainant is otherwise entitled to and is fully paid;
(c) restrain the respondent from reporting on the work performance of the complainant, or from writing
their confidential report or appraisal, and assign that responsibility to another person; or
(d) grant such other relief as may be appropriate.
Nexora implements a recommendation for interim relief within five (5) working days. Interim relief is
protective and is not a finding against the respondent.
11.6 Conduct of the Inquiry
 1. The inquiry is conducted in accordance with the principles of natural justice.
2. Both parties are given a fair opportunity to be heard, to present documents, to name
witnesses, and to respond to the material relied upon.
 3. Neither party may bring a legal practitioner to represent them before the IC
(Rule 7(6)). A party may be accompanied by a colleague of their choice who is not a witness in the matter.
 4. The parties are not permitted to cross-examine each other directly. Questions are put
through the IC.
 5. A minimum of three (3) members, including the Presiding Officer, must be present at every
hearing (Section 11(3) proviso).
 6. Where either party fails, without sufficient cause, to attend three consecutive hearings,

the IC may, after giving fifteen (15) days' written notice, terminate the proceedings or give an ex parte
decision.
 7. All proceedings are recorded in minutes signed by the members present. Recordings by any
party are prohibited.
 8. The standard of proof is the balance of probabilities.
11.7 Findings and Recommendations
Where the IC concludes that the allegation is not proved, it recommends that no action be taken and
records its reasons. A finding that an allegation is not proved is not a finding that the complaint was false or
malicious.
Where the IC concludes that the allegation is proved, it recommends:
 (a) action in accordance with this Policy and the service rules, which may include a written warning, a
warning entered on the personnel record, withholding of promotion, withholding of an increment,
withholding of variable pay, counselling, community service, suspension, or termination of service; and
(b) deduction from the respondent's salary or wages of such sum as it considers appropriate to be paid to
the complainant or to their legal heirs, having regard to the mental trauma, pain, suffering and emotional
distress caused; the medical expenses incurred; the loss of career opportunity; the income and financial
status of the respondent; and the feasibility of payment in a lump sum or in instalments (Sections
13(3)(ii) and 15).
Where the respondent is not an employee — a contractor, a client employee, a vendor — the IC
recommends action available under the contract, which may include removal from the engagement,
revocation of site access, escalation to the respondent's employer, and referral to the police.
11.8 Malicious Complaints
Where the IC concludes that a complaint was made maliciously, or that the complainant or a witness
knowingly produced a forged or misleading document, it may recommend action against that person
(Section 14).
The IC must record its reasons, and an inquiry into the malice must be conducted before any
recommendation is made. The mere inability to substantiate a complaint, or the absence of adequate
proof, does not attract this clause. Nexora will not treat an unproved complaint as a false complaint, and
no adverse entry is made against a complainant whose complaint is not proved.
11.9 Confidentiality
The contents of the complaint, the identity and addresses of the complainant, the respondent and the
witnesses, any information relating to the conciliation and inquiry proceedings, and the recommendations
and action taken must not be published, communicated or made known to the public, the press or the
media in any manner (Section 16).
Breach of confidentiality by any person, including an IC member, attracts a penalty under Section 17 and is
serious misconduct under this Code. Information may be disclosed only to the extent required to implement
the recommendations, to comply with the law, or to respond to a lawful order.

The IC maintains its records in a locked cabinet and an access-controlled repository administered by the
Presiding Officer, separate from PeopleHub and inaccessible to HR Operations, the reporting managers or
the ELT.
11.10 Prohibition of Retaliation
No person may victimise, intimidate or retaliate against a complainant, a witness, an IC member, or any
person who assists in an inquiry. Retaliation includes an adverse change to rating, allocation,
compensation, working conditions or reporting line, exclusion, or social ostracism.
Retaliation is a distinct and serious misconduct, is inquired into separately, and attracts consequences up
to termination irrespective of the outcome of the underlying complaint.
11.11 Right to Criminal Proceedings
Nothing in this Policy prevents a complainant from initiating criminal proceedings. Where the conduct
complained of constitutes an offence under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, or any other law, the IC
informs the complainant of their right to initiate action, and, at the complainant's request, assists in doing
so. Where the complainant chooses to file a police complaint, the internal inquiry continues unless the IC
determines that it should be stayed.

1. Purpose and Scope
1.1 Purpose
This Policy sets out how Nexora Technologies Private Limited determines, structures, administers and
pays compensation and benefits. It exists so that pay decisions are consistent, explainable, compliant and
defensible, and so that every employee can understand how their own pay is constructed and when it will
reach their account.
1.2 Scope
This Policy applies to all employees on the Nexora payroll at Gurugram, Bengaluru and Pune, including
probationers, Graduate Engineer Trainees and fixed-term contract employees, except where a clause
states otherwise. It does not apply to independent contractors, consultants engaged on a statement of
work, or staffing-partner deputees, whose remuneration is governed by the relevant contract.
1.3 Compensation Philosophy
Nexora's compensation philosophy rests on five commitments:
 1. Market-informed. Fixed pay is benchmarked annually against the Indian IT services
market using the Aon and Mercer India Technology surveys, with Nexora targeting the 60th percentile of
the peer set for Band B1–B4 and the 50th percentile for Band B5 and above, where the mix shifts towards
variable pay.
 2. Internally equitable. Two employees in the same band, role family, location and
performance tier should be paid within a defensible range of each other. Compa-ratio dispersion is
reviewed annually.
 3. Performance-differentiated. Increment and variable pay outcomes differ materially by
rating. A rating of 5 must produce a visibly different outcome from a rating of 3.
 4. Transparent in structure. Every employee can see how their CTC is constructed, what
each component means, and how each is taxed.
 5. Compliant without exception. Statutory obligations under the Employees' Provident
Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952, the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, the Payment of Bonus
Act, 1965, the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, the Income-tax Act, 1961, the Employees' State Insurance
Act, 1948 and applicable State Professional Tax legislation are met in full and on time.
1.4 Pay Equity
Nexora conducts an annual pay equity review, completed before the increment cycle closes, comparing
median fixed pay by gender within each band, role family and location cohort of ten or more. Any
unexplained gap above 3% is corrected in the same cycle through a targeted adjustment budget held by
the CHRO, outside the function's increment pool. The result of the review is reported to the Board's
Nomination and Remuneration Committee each year.

4.2 Calculation
 Variable payout = Variable pay opportunity × Company multiplier × Business unit multiplier ×
Individual multiplier × Eligibility fraction
 Company multiplier (0.6 to 1.3) is determined by the Board against the annual revenue and EBITDA
plan.
 Business unit multiplier (0.7 to 1.3) is determined by the ELT against the business unit's revenue,
margin, utilisation and client satisfaction targets.
 Individual multiplier is the rating multiplier from Clause 3.2.
 Eligibility fraction is the proportion of the assessment year (1 April to 31 March) for which the
employee was on the payroll and not on unpaid leave, expressed to two decimals.
Worked example: a Band B4 employee on CTC INR 30,00,000, rated 4, who joined on 1 October 2025, in a
year where the Company multiplier is 0.95 and the business unit multiplier is 1.10.
 Opportunity = 12% × 30,00,000 = INR 3,60,000 Payout = 3,60,000 × 0.95 × 1.10 × 1.20 × 0.50 = INR
2,25,720
4.3 Eligibility and Exclusions
An employee is not eligible for variable pay where they have resigned, are serving notice, or have been
served notice of termination on the date of disbursement; where they hold a rating of 1; where they are on a
live final written warning under HR-POL-001, Clause 15.2; or where they are on a Performance
Improvement Plan that has not been successfully closed.
Employees on Maternity, Paternity or Adoption Leave during the assessment year are treated as being on
the payroll for the full period of that leave, and the leave does not reduce the eligibility fraction.
Variable pay is discretionary. Payment in one year creates no entitlement in any subsequent year.

11. Frequently Asked Questions
Q1. My CTC is INR 24,00,000. Why is my monthly credit not INR 2,00,000? Because CTC includes
variable pay and retirals, which are not part of the monthly cash salary, and because statutory and tax
deductions are made from the fixed monthly amount. See the worked example at Clause 2.3.
Q2. When will I get my increment letter? Letters are released on 25 June and the revision is effective 1
July, appearing first in the July payroll credited on the last working day of July.
Q3. I joined in February 2026. Am I eligible for the July 2026 increment? No. Employees joining on or
after 1 April of the assessment year are not eligible in the immediately following cycle. Employees joining
between 1 January and 31 March receive 50% of the guideline.
Q4. I resigned on 10 May. Will I receive variable pay in June? No. Employees who have resigned or are
serving notice on the date of disbursement are not eligible.
Q5. Can I add my parents to the medical policy in September? Only if you joined in the preceding thirty
days or have had a qualifying life event. Otherwise you must wait for the renewal on 1 July.
Q6. How long is my notice period? Sixty calendar days if you are at Band B1 to B3, and ninety calendar
days at Band B4 and above. Thirty calendar days during probation.
Q7. I did not submit investment proofs in January. What happens? The provisional declaration is
withdrawn and tax is recomputed without those deductions, with the shortfall recovered from the February
and March payrolls. You may still claim the deduction when you file your return of income.
Q8. Why is my professional tax INR 300 in February? Maharashtra levies INR 200 for ten months and
INR 300 in February, totalling INR 2,500 for the year. Haryana does not levy professional tax at all.

3. The Employment Relationship
3.1 Categories of Employment
3.1.1 Permanent employees are engaged without a fixed end date, subject to the notice provisions in
Clause 16.1. They are eligible for the full benefits set out in Clause 7.
3.1.2 Probationers are permanent employees who have not yet been confirmed. All new hires, whether
fresher or lateral, serve a probation period of six (6) months from the date of joining. Probation may be
extended once, by a maximum of three (3) months, by the reporting manager with the written concurrence
of the HR Business Partner and the Band B6-or-above function head.
3.1.3 Fixed-term contract employees are engaged for a defined period, ordinarily between six and
twenty-four months, against a funded client engagement. Fixed-term contracts do not renew automatically.
Statutory benefits (Provident Fund, ESI where applicable, gratuity where the statutory service condition is
met) apply in full.
3.1.4 Graduate Engineer Trainees (GETs) are campus hires enrolled in Nexora Launchpad. GETs serve
a training period of eight (8) weeks followed by a probation of six (6) months from the date of deployment to
a project. GET appointments carry a service commitment of eighteen (18) months from the date of joining,
as recorded in the GET appointment letter.
3.1.5 Interns are engaged for a period of eight to twenty-four weeks against a defined project. Interns
receive a stipend, are not on the benefits programme, and are covered by the Company's Group Personal
Accident policy only.
3.2 Recruitment and Selection
Recruitment is conducted by the Talent Acquisition team under the Head of Talent Acquisition. Every open
role must have an approved Position Requisition on PeopleHub carrying (i) the budget code, (ii) the band,
(iii) the location, and (iv) the approval of the function head and, for any position at Band B5 and above, of
the Chief Financial Officer.
Nexora is an equal opportunity employer. Selection is on merit alone. The Company does not discriminate
on the basis of religion, race, caste, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, place of birth, descent, marital
status, pregnancy, disability, age or any other status protected by law. Interview panels for Band B4 and
above must include at least one member from a different function than the hiring manager.
Employee referrals. Nexora encourages referrals. Referral awards are set out in Clause 7.7. Employees
must not participate in any stage of the selection process for a candidate they have referred, nor for any
relative as defined in Section 2(77) of the Companies Act, 2013.

4. Working Hours, Attendance and Workplace Model
4.1 The Standard Work Week
The standard work week at Nexora is Monday to Friday. The standard working day is nine (9) hours,
inclusive of a sixty (60) minute unpaid meal break and two paid rest breaks of fifteen (15) minutes each.
This gives a net working time of eight (8) hours per day and forty (40) hours per week.
Saturdays and Sundays are weekly offs. Where a client engagement requires a different weekly pattern —
for example a Sunday-to-Thursday week for a Gulf-region client — the pattern is documented in the
engagement's Delivery Operating Model and approved by the Delivery Manager and HRBP. In no case will
an employee be scheduled for more than six consecutive working days without a weekly off.
4.2 Flexible Start and Core Hours
Nexora operates a flexible start window. Employees may begin work at any time between 08:00 and 11:00
IST, provided they complete their net eight hours and are available during core hours of 11:00 to 17:00
IST. Core hours are when meetings, stand-ups, design reviews and client calls are scheduled. Employees
must not schedule recurring internal meetings outside core hours without the agreement of every required
attendee.
Flexibility is a facility, not an entitlement, and may be restricted at project level where a client's contracted
service window requires it. Any such restriction must be recorded in the engagement's Delivery Operating
Model.
4.3 Attendance Recording
Attendance is recorded in two ways, both of which are mandatory:
 1. Access-card swipe at the turnstiles on entry to and exit from the office floor. The
first swipe of the day and the last swipe of the day define the in-office duration.
 2. PeopleHub check-in, completed from the Nexora network or through the PeopleHub
mobile application with location services enabled.
